sentences.text: Choose line by what it needs to do.
Nylon is strong and stretchy, so it absorbs shock loads, which makes it ideal for anchor rodes, dock lines and towlines.
Polyester, often sold as Dacron, is strong with little stretch, used for halyards and sheets.
Polypropylene floats, which makes it useful for ring buoy lines and ski ropes, but it’s weaker and breaks down in sunlight.
Spectra and Dyneema are extremely strong, low-stretch, floating fibers used in specialty lines.
